ateret-zekenim/part-001.txt.6:_: Women are not [included in zimun], etc. And our teacher Rabbi Simcha would act to add a woman; and also you should know that a woman is only obligated d'rabbanan—that is to exclude discharging others; but for mere combination for mention of our God they combine well, several times from Maharshal in his name; and I never heard a place that practiced thus — Hagur.
ateret-zekenim/part-001.txt.10:_: A minor who reached [the age], etc. And some say specifically only if the minor is at least eight or seven years old, for that is the time of his education; but a minor of six—even if he is sharp and knows to whom they bless and to whom they pray—counts for nothing, for he has not reached the season of toddlers and he is like one without da'at (She'elot u-Teshuvot Rashba and Rivash). And specifically one minor is combined for three, but not two—for we require a majority of adults; but for ten he may combine, even three minors, as three vegetable eaters combine (Kol Bo).

baer-heitev/part-001.txt.4:_: And did not immerse. And whenever he did not immerse properly he is called one who did not immerse. And it is obvious that one who is wicked publicly and transgresses sins—and all the more a mumar—we do not invite zimun on him, for he is no worse than am ha'aretz in Talmudic times — Magen Avraham. And a mumar who repented—even if he did not immerse—may combine; see Yoreh Deah end of siman 268.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.5:_: Onen. Meaning: whenever his dead lies before him; see siman 71.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.6:_: Among themselves. See in Sefer Yad Eliyahu daf 109 folio 3.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.10:א: The toddlers. About six or seven years old; and Magen Avraham wrote about nine or ten years old—see there; perhaps it is a printing error.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.10:ב: Two hairs. Meaning: one need not check for two hairs; but if we do not know that he produced two hairs, we do not invite zimun on him. And to discharge others we require that we know certainly he produced two hairs; however if each blesses for himself silently—we do not care—see siman 156 s.k. 8 Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.10:ג: And deaf. Specifically a deaf-mute who speaks and does not hear; and a fool who is not a complete fool—see Levush. Magen Avraham.

beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.2:_: Rif and Rosh there, end of chapter 8 of Chullin.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.3:_: Tosafot there in Berachot 47, in the Rosh.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.4:ב: Tosafot in the name of R' Yitzchak in Bava Batra, and so the consensus of poskim.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.6:ב: Rambam chapter 5 halacha 5 of Laws of Berachot.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.7:_: Semag in the name of R' Yitzchak from that in Arachin 2.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.8:_: From that Rosh Hashanah 29 regarding shofar.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.11:_: Rivash in responsa and other poskim; see in siman 55.

beur-hagra/part-001.txt.3:_: Seif 3 am ha'aretz, etc. Tosafot there s.v. ar"h, see there.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ב: But [convert], etc. We learn from the above.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ג: And to say [al shehinchalta], etc. Tosafot Bava Batra chapter 1 folio 1 s.v. lema'utei, etc.; and for R' Yitzchak it appears, etc.; as written above siman 53 seif 9.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ד: Seif 6 but, etc., and not, etc. Gemara there 2b.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ה: Provided that, etc. For they do not combine for all who require ten, learned from venikdashti, etc.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ו: Seif 7 women, etc. Tosafot there s.v. she'ani, etc.; and so too in Arachin 3a s.v. mezamenot, etc.; and it should be said, etc.; and the Rosh challenged them—for in Arachin there they say all are obligated, etc., like priests, Levites, and Israelites; and Semag explains that there when women eat with men, as we wrote; and it should be said that what we wrote—that braita women, etc.—therefore when they eat with men they are obligated; and it is forced; and the Rosh's words are primary; and so Terumat HaDeshen see there.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ז: And they fulfill [through our zimun], etc. For the doubt in the Gemara 2b is only whether women discharge the men.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ח: Even though, etc. In responsa 193 not so—and it requires study; and perhaps his view is as Taz wrote there—and it requires study.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ט: Seif 8 androgynous, etc.; tumtum, etc. Tosefta of Berachot there.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:י: Seif 10 minor, etc. From what is written—a minor who knows, etc.; and less than the season of toddlers has no da'at, as written in tractate Nezikin and chapter 3—and not like R' Chaim who wrote specifically a minor porach who entered year thirteen and a youth.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:כ: Whether [for three or ten], etc. Not like R' Hillel Gaon who wrote specifically for ten; and as R' Yehoshua ben Levi said regarding a minor lying in a cradle; and so in Jerusalem Talmud there—R' Yaakov bar Zavdi asked before R' Yosi son of R' Eliezer: there they make him a branch for ten—they say, so too they make him a branch for three; what is there that they mention the Name—they make him a branch for ten; here where they do not mention the Name—all the more he said to him—and is it not all the more there—since they mention the Name they make him a branch for ten; here where they do not mention the Name they do not make him a branch; but the Rambam holds that all this is regarding a minor lying in a cradle, but a minor like this there is no distinction; and so is implied in the Gemara that says R' Yehoshua ben Levi—even though they said, etc.—apparently this inviting zimun is for three; and on this R' Yosi and Ran—that they invite zimun for a minor like this; and Tosafot there s.v. veleit, etc.; and Raavad, etc.; nevertheless the Rambam does not hold like Raavad, since it says veleit halakhta kekhol, etc., 41—even like R' Yehoshua ben Levi.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:ל: And some say, etc. Tosafot above; however it says in Jerusalem Talmud R' Yirmiyah, etc.; and this is our teacher's language, etc.—meaning we do not practice until he brings two hairs, as Tosafot wrote there 41—that to combine for zimun we do not practice, etc.—even though in our Gemara 41 even for practical action that Abbaye and Rava say, etc.; and Tosafot there s.v. Abbaye, etc.; and so per the Rif's view who explained that he must reach the season of toddlers.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:מ: Then, etc. As written above siman 35 seif 5 in Hagahah.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.4:נ: Seif 11 one whom they excommunicated, etc. As written there seif 11 and seif 12.

biur-halacha/part-001.txt.3:א: Am ha'aretz complete, etc.—See in Mishna Berurah what he wrote that all the more so if he is a complete wicked person transgressing sins publicly we do not invite zimun on him; and see in Peri Megadim who wrote there is no contradiction to this from seif 11, which explains there specifically when they excommunicated him for a sin, but otherwise we invite zimun on him—for there it is one sin and here he transgressed many sins; and in my humble opinion it appears there is no distinction in the matter, but for other holy matters such as Torah reading and kedusha and other holy matters requiring ten—certainly even if he transgressed many sins for appetite, as long as they did not excommunicate him he counts toward the number ten—for so is implied from the Mechaber's conclusion above siman 55 seif 11 see there [and also the proof they brought there from Achan that it is written in him Yisrael has sinned—even though he sinned he is Yisrael—also teaches thus, for there there was chillul Shabbat and several other transgressions]; and here for zimun it is reasonable that even if he transgressed one sin publicly b'mezid [such as he ate pig or nevelah and terefah which is a matter publicized among Israel as forbidden] we do not invite zimun on him; and the reason is that the matter of zimun is that his obligation comes because at first they joined together for eating and therefore likewise afterward they need to join to bless Hashem blessed be He on the eating they ate; and on this it says in the Mishnah that if he is am ha'aretz we do not invite zimun on him—and that is because he was negligent in not learning—therefore one does not join with him to invite zimun as the poskim wrote; and therefore Magen Avraham says if he is wicked and transgresses the Torah publicly certainly it is not proper to join with him for zimun [and seif 11 does not deal with such a case]; and by inference it is reasonable that even if they saw him once publicly who denied a sin likewise one does not invite zimun with him. And know that for zimun they were much stricter—for behold certainly even a complete am ha'aretz they combine for ten for kaddish and Barchu and the like; and for zimun it says in the Mishnah we do not invite zimun on him—or that for zimun it is much stricter and as we wrote the reason. And according to all this what is stated above in siman 55 that if they did not excommunicate him he combines for the number ten—that is only for other matters requiring ten; but for zimun with the Name certainly not—for he is no better than am ha'aretz in Talmudic times; and nevertheless it was possible to say further that what the Mishnah says am ha'aretz we do not invite zimun on him—that is specifically for three; but for adding a branch to ten they do make; and according to this the law of Magen Avraham regarding a wicked person who transgresses publicly is also specifically for three and not for ten. And according to this what is stated in Shulchan Aruch above in siman 55 that he counts for ten—is even for zimun with the Name—and it requires study.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.3:ב: We invite zimun on him in this time—See in Mishna Berurah s.k. 2; and all this is regarding whether we combine him for zimun on him; and the reason that because he was negligent in not learning—from the Gemara's law one does not join with him to combine him for zimun, as the Rosh wrote; and all the more so if he does not fulfill mitzvot of the Torah this reason applies; but he himself is certainly obligated in zimun like other Israelites [and there is practical difference whether three such were obligated to invite zimun, or if he sat in a company of fit men who were three besides him—certainly he is not permitted to separate from them and invite them] for one who ate garlic and his odor wafts, etc., and as Rambam wrote in a responsum that even Yerovam ben Nevat who worshipped idols nevertheless is punished also for light matters such as eruv tavshilin and the like; and so is proven in Tosafot Chagigah 22 s.v. keman in the Beit HaSafek see there; afterward I found so too in Shitah Mekubetzet Berachot see there.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.7:א: Women invite zimun among themselves—permission; and the Gra's view in his Biur is that the primary law is like the Rosh and Terumat HaDeshen that women inviting zimun among themselves is an obligation; but the world did not practice thus.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.7:ב: But when they eat with the men—obviously even one woman.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.7:ג: And they fulfill through our zimun—and it is implied from the words of the small hand that she is forbidden to recite the berachah of zimun and discharge the men, but she must hear and fulfill through the zimun the men bless.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.8:_: He invites zimun with his kind—and whether it is reshut or chovah see Eshel Avraham and Levush and Rabbi Akiva Eiger.
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.10:א: Until he is thirteen years old—and meaning even if he brought hairs before thirteen it does not help [Magen Avraham and so Perishah and Bach].
biur-halacha/part-001.txt.10:ב: They combine for zimun—See in Mishna Berurah that it deals with a deaf-mute who speaks and does not hear. It seems simply that specifically for combination; but it is not proper l'chatchila that he be the one inviting zimun to discharge others in birkat hamazon—for we hold in siman 185 seif 2 that l'chatchila he must make heard to his ear; and if so, even though hearing is like answering, nevertheless they are not better than he himself—and berachot remain with them in speech alone without hearing to the ears. Afterward I found in Chiddushei Ra'ah who also wrote thus regarding that it is not worthwhile that he be shaliach tzibur l'chatchila also for this reason see there. And behold when the invitees discharge in birkat hamazon certainly so it is; but as today when they do not discharge in birkat hamazon at all and each blesses for himself and the inviter says only n'varech alone—it is possible to be lenient that he too be the inviter l'chatchila, and it is not comparable to prayer; for even in our time each blesses for himself—nevertheless what the shaliach tzibur repeats in prayer, even though he already prayed himself before, is because the enactment of the Sages did not move from its place; not so here, where the responders who say Baruch she'achalnu, etc.—behold they make heard to their ears; and what difference is it to us if one who says n'varech cannot make heard to his ear—and it requires study.
